First: We test him.

Second: We charge him with work.

Second: We test his gratitude in ease and his patience in hardship. This was said by al-Hasan.

First: work after creation. This was said by Muqatil.

Second: religion, so that he is commanded to obey and forbidden from disobedience.

First: he hears with his two ears and sees with his two eyes, as a favour of blessing upon him.

Second: guidance away from error. This was said by Ikrima.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on Surah 76, verses 4–12:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink﴾ There are two opinions regarding "the righteous" (al-abrar):

The first is that they are the truthful. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second is that they are the obedient. This was said by Muqatil. (p-165)

There are three opinions regarding why they were called "righteous" (abrar):
The first is that they were so named because they were dutiful to their fathers and sons. This was said by Ibn Umar.

The second is that they restrained harm. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third is that they fulfilled the right of Allah and kept their vows. This was said by Qatada.

As for His words ﴿from a cup﴾, it means wine. al-Dahhak said: "Every 'cup' (ka's) in the Qur'an refers to wine."

Regarding His words ﴿whose mixture is camphor﴾, there are two opinions:

The first is that Kafur is a spring in Paradise named Kafur. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second is that it is the camphor of perfume. Based on this, there are three opinions on what is intended by its mixing into the cup:
The first is its coolness. al-Hasan said: "[It is mixed] with the coolness of camphor and the taste of ginger."

The second is its fragrance. Qatada said: "It is mixed with camphor and sealed with musk."

The third is its taste. al-Suddi said: "Its taste is as if it were the taste of camphor."

﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾, meaning the friends of Allah, because the disbeliever does not drink from it at all, even if he is one of the servants of Allah. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is that the servants of Allah benefit from it. This was said by al-Farra'.

The second is that the servants of Allah drink from it.

Muqatil said: "It is Tasnim, and it is the most noble drink of Paradise. The ones brought near [to Allah] drink from it pure, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise with wine, milk and honey."

﴿They make it gush forth in abundance﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is that they lead it wherever they wish in Paradise. This was said by Mujahid.

The second is that they mix it with whatever they wish. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also bear a third interpretation: that they extract it from wherever they wish in Paradise.

Regarding His words ﴿in abundance﴾ (tafjiran), there are two interpretations: (p-166)

The first is that it is a verbal noun intended to indicate abundance.

The second is that they make it gush from those springs into more springs, so that it is more enjoyable and more expansive.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first is that they fulfil what Allah has made obligatory upon them of His worship. This was said by Qatada.

The second is that they fulfil what they have pledged upon themselves of the right of Allah. This was said by Mujahid.

The third is that they fulfil the covenant to those with whom they made a covenant. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The fourth is that they fulfil their oaths when they swear by them. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also bear a fifth interpretation: that they fulfil what they were warned of, of His threat.

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil is widespread﴾. al-Kalbi said: "[It is] the punishment of a Day whose evil is widespread." Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is that it is widespread (fashiyan). This was said by Ibn Abbas and al-Akhfash.

The second is that it is extended (mumtaddan). This was said by al-Farra', and from it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"She departed, and she had left in the heart a split, despite her distance, widespread."

That is, extended.

It may also bear a third interpretation, meaning swift.

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

The first is "despite their love for the food." This was said by Muqatil.

The second is "despite their desire for it." This was said by al-Kalbi.

The third is "despite its scarcity." This was said by Qutrub.

﴿to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. Regarding the captive there are three opinions:
The first is that he is the Muslim prisoner. This was said by Mujahid.

The second is that he is the slave. This was said by Ikrimah.

The third is the captive of the polytheists. This was said by al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Then the ruling concerning the captive of the polytheists was abrogated (naskh) by the sword." Others said: "Rather, it remains in force regarding the captive, [the obligation being] to feed him, unless the Imam sees fit to kill him."

It may also bear a fourth interpretation: that by "the captive" is meant one whose mind is deficient, since he is held captive by his madness and insanity. And the captivity of the polytheists is retaliation, which depends upon the opinion of the Imam, whereas this [feeding] is righteousness and kindness.

﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah﴾. Mujahid said: "They did not actually say this, but Allah knew it from them and praised them, so that whoever desires it may be encouraged to do the same."

﴿We do not want from you any reward or thanks﴾. Reward refers to deeds, and thanks refers to words. It was also said that this verse was revealed concerning those who took responsibility for the captives of Badr. They were seven from among the Muhajirun: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, al-Zubayr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'id and Abu Ubayda.

﴿Indeed we fear from our Lord a Day that is grim and distressing﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

The first is that the grimness (ubus) is what contorts the faces from its evil, and the qamtarir is severe. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second is that the grimness is constriction, and the qamtarir is lengthy. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The poet said:

"Severe, grim, distressing, you think of him
as the forenoon departs, the humps of the shoulders [are shaking]."

The third is that the grimness is with the lips, and the qamtarir is with the forehead and the eyebrows. Thus it is made one of the attributes of a face that changes from the hardships of that Day. This was said by Mujahid. Ibn al-A'rabi recited:

"He goes out to the hunt, returning with a broken [spirit],
he frowns for a while and then scowls."

﴿So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day and gave them radiance and joy﴾. al-Hasan said: "Radiance (nadrah) is in the faces, and joy is in the hearts."

Regarding radiance there are three interpretations:

The first is that it is whiteness and brightness. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second is that it is beauty and splendour. This was said by Ibn Jubayr. (p-168)

The third is that it is the trace of blessing. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

﴿And He rewarded them for what they endured﴾. This may bear two interpretations:

The first is for what they endured in obedience to Allah.

The second is for what they endured in fulfilling the vow.

﴿a garden and silk﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is a garden in which they dwell, and silk which they wear.

The second is that the garden is the dwelling place, and the silk is the lasting of life in Paradise. From it comes the wearing of silk: "they will be adorned (yulbasuna) with the pleasure of living."

It has been disputed concerning who this verse was revealed about, and there are two opinions:

The first is what al-Dahhak related from Jabir, that it was revealed concerning Mut'im ibn Warqa' al-Ansari, who made a vow and fulfilled it.

The second is what Amr related from al-Hasan, that it was revealed concerning Ali and Fatima, may Allah be pleased with them both. The reason is that Ali and Fatima vowed to fast and then fulfilled it. Fatima baked three loaves of barley so that Ali could break his fast with one of them, she with another, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn would eat the third. A needy man asked her, and she gave him one of them as charity. Then an orphan asked her, and she gave him the second. Then a captive asked her, and she gave him the third. And they spent the night hungry.

﴿They make it gush forth in abundance﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is that they lead it wherever they wish in Paradise. This was said by Mujahid.

The second is that they mix it with whatever they wish. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also bear a third interpretation: that they extract it from wherever they wish in Paradise.

Regarding His words ﴿in abundance﴾ (tafjiran), there are two interpretations: (p-166)

The first is that it is a verbal noun intended to indicate abundance.

The second is that they make it gush from those springs into more springs, so that it is more enjoyable and more expansive.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first is that they fulfil what Allah has made obligatory upon them of His worship. This was said by Qatada.

The second is that they fulfil what they have pledged upon themselves of the right of Allah. This was said by Mujahid.

The third is that they fulfil the covenant to those with whom they made a covenant. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The fourth is that they fulfil their oaths when they swear by them. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also bear a fifth interpretation: that they fulfil what they were warned of, of His threat.

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil is widespread﴾. al-Kalbi said: "[It is] the punishment of a Day whose evil is widespread." Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is that it is widespread (fashiyan). This was said by Ibn Abbas and al-Akhfash.

The second is that it is extended (mumtaddan). This was said by al-Farra', and from it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"She departed, and she had left in the heart a split, despite her distance, widespread."

That is, extended.

It may also bear a third interpretation, meaning swift.

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

The first is "despite their love for the food." This was said by Muqatil.

The second is "despite their desire for it." This was said by al-Kalbi.

The third is "despite its scarcity." This was said by Qutrub.

﴿to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. Regarding the captive there are three opinions:
The first is that he is the Muslim prisoner. This was said by Mujahid.

The second is that he is the slave. This was said by Ikrimah.

The third is the captive of the polytheists. This was said by al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Then the ruling concerning the captive of the polytheists was abrogated (naskh) by the sword." Others said: "Rather, it remains in force regarding the captive, [the obligation being] to feed him, unless the Imam sees fit to kill him."

It may also bear a fourth interpretation: that by "the captive" is meant one whose mind is deficient, since he is held captive by his madness and insanity. And the captivity of the polytheists is retaliation, which depends upon the opinion of the Imam, whereas this [feeding] is righteousness and kindness.

﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah﴾. Mujahid said: "They did not actually say this, but Allah knew it from them and praised them, so that whoever desires it may be encouraged to do the same."

﴿We do not want from you any reward or thanks﴾. Reward refers to deeds, and thanks refers to words. It was also said that this verse was revealed concerning those who took responsibility for the captives of Badr. They were seven from among the Muhajirun: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, al-Zubayr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'id and Abu Ubayda.

﴿Indeed we fear from our Lord a Day that is grim and distressing﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

The first is that the grimness (ubus) is what contorts the faces from its evil, and the qamtarir is severe. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second is that the grimness is constriction, and the qamtarir is lengthy. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The poet said:

"Severe, grim, distressing, you think of him
as the forenoon departs, the humps of the shoulders [are shaking]."

The third is that the grimness is with the lips, and the qamtarir is with the forehead and the eyebrows. Thus it is made one of the attributes of a face that changes from the hardships of that Day. This was said by Mujahid. Ibn al-A'rabi recited:

"He goes out to the hunt, returning with a broken [spirit],
he frowns for a while and then scowls."

﴿So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day and gave them radiance and joy﴾. al-Hasan said: "Radiance (nadrah) is in the faces, and joy is in the hearts."

Regarding radiance there are three interpretations:

The first is that it is whiteness and brightness. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second is that it is beauty and splendour. This was said by Ibn Jubayr. (p-168)

The third is that it is the trace of blessing. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

﴿And He rewarded them for what they endured﴾. This may bear two interpretations:

The first is for what they endured in obedience to Allah.

The second is for what they endured in fulfilling the vow.

﴿a garden and silk﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first is a garden in which they dwell, and silk which they wear.

The second is that the garden is the dwelling place, and the silk is the lasting of life in Paradise. From it comes the wearing of silk: "they will be adorned (yulbasuna) with the pleasure of living."

It has been disputed concerning who this verse was revealed about, and there are two opinions:

The first is what al-Dahhak related from Jabir, that it was revealed concerning Mut'im ibn Warqa' al-Ansari, who made a vow and fulfilled it.

The second is what Amr related from al-Hasan, that it was revealed concerning Ali and Fatima, may Allah be pleased with them both. The reason is that Ali and Fatima vowed to fast and then fulfilled it. Fatima baked three loaves of barley so that Ali could break his fast with one of them, she with another, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn would eat the third. A needy man asked her, and she gave him one of them as charity. Then an orphan asked her, and she gave him the second. Then a captive asked her, and she gave him the third. And they spent the night hungry.

[p. 169] ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Along with what we have already said about its interpretation, there are two opinions:

One: they are beds. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: they are everything one reclines upon. This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾. As for what is meant by "sun," there are two views:

One: they will be in a lasting light that needs no other light, so the absence of the sun is an intensification in describing the light.

The second: they will not see a sun there, so they will not be harmed by its heat, and its absence is a negation of its harm.

As for "zamharir" (bitter cold), there are three views:

The first: it is intense cold. 'Ikrimah said this, because they will not experience heat or cold in Paradise.

The second: it is a color in the punishment. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

The third: it is the moon, from this same root. Tha'lab said this and recited:

"A night whose darkness has thickened, I crossed it, and the zamharir had not appeared."

It is also narrated as "ma zahar" (that had not shone). Its meaning is that they will be in a lasting light with neither night nor day, because the light of day is from the sun and the light of night is from the moon.

﴿And its fruit-clusters will be lowered within easy reach﴾. There are two views concerning this:

One: no thorn or distance will prevent their hands from reaching it. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: when one stands, it rises, and when one sits, it descends. This is the view of Mujahid. [p. 170]

It may also bear a third meaning: that the lowering of its clusters is that they emerge for them from their sheaths and are freed from their pits.

﴿And cups that are crystal-clear﴾, ﴿crystal-clear, made of silver﴾. As for the cups, we have already mentioned what they are among the vessels.

Concerning His words, Exalted is He, ﴿crystal-clear, made of silver﴾, there are two views:

One: they are of silver, owing to the clarity of crystal. This is the view of al-Sha'bi.

The second: they are of crystal, in the whiteness of silver. This is the view of Abu Salih.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the crystal of every land is from its soil, and the land of Paradise is silver, which is why its crystal is silver.

﴿They will determine its measure﴾. Concerning this there are five sayings:

The first: they determined it in themselves, and it came according to what they determined. This is the view of al-Hasan.

The second: according to the measure of the palm's fullness. This is the view of al-Dahhak.

The third: at an amount that does not overflow, nor fall short and become scant. This is the view of Mujahid.

The fourth: according to the measure of their satisfaction and sufficiency, because that is more pleasant and more delightful. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

The fifth: it was measured out for them, and they measured it equally. This is the view of al-Sha'bi.

﴿And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture is ginger﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

One: it is mixed with ginger, which the Arabs find pleasing, because it loosens the tongue and aids digestion. This is the view of al-Suddi and Ibn Abi Najih.

The second: "Zanjabil" (ginger) is the name of the spring from which the drink of the righteous is mixed. This is the view of Mujahid.

The third: "zanjabil" is one of the flavors of wine, which leaves a pleasure after drinking it. Ibn Shajarah related this, and from it is the poet's saying:

"And it is as if the taste of ginger in it, when I tasted it, and the purest wine..."

﴿A spring therein called Salsabil﴾. Concerning this there are six sayings:

The first: it is its name. This is the view of 'Ikrimah.

The second: its meaning is "ask for a path to it." This is the view of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

The third: it means "the chain of the path." This is the view of Mujahid.

The fourth: it is a chain they direct wherever they wish. This is the view of Qatadah.

The fifth: that it slips down their throats smoothly. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The sixth: that it is the one that flows freshly. This is also the view of Mujahid, and from it is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit:

"They give to drink to whoever comes to al-Bariş among them a cup that shimmers with smooth, pure wine."

Muqatil said: it was called Salsabil because it slips over them in their gatherings, their chambers, and their paths.

﴿And there will circle around them youths made eternal﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

One: "made eternal" means they never die. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: they are young children who never grow up, and youths who never grow old. This is the view of al-Dahhak and al-Hasan.

The third: that is, adorned with bracelets. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, and the poet said:

"And eternal maidens with silver ornaments, as if their hindquarters were the dunes' sand-hills."

﴿When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls﴾. Concerning this there are two sayings:

One: they are likened to scattered pearls because of their great number. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: because of the purity of their complexions and the beauty of their appearance. This is the meaning of the saying of Sufyan.

﴿And when you look there﴾, meaning Paradise, ﴿you will see bliss﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: it means abundance of blessing. [p. 172]

The second: abundance of delight.

﴿And a great dominion﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: because of its vastness and abundance.

The second: because the angels seek permission to enter upon them and greet them with peace.

It may also bear a third meaning: that they will not desire anything without being able to attain it.

﴿And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

One: it is described as such because they do not urinate from it nor do they pass wind from it. This is the view of 'Atiyyah. Ibrahim al-Taymi said: it is a sweat that flows from their bodies, like the scent of musk.

The second: because the wine of Paradise is pure, whereas the wine of this world is impure, and therefore Allah, Exalted is He, described it as pure. Ibn Shajarah said this.

The third: that the rivers of Paradise contain nothing impure, as is the case in the rivers and lands of this world. Ibn 'Isa related this.
